short: Recognizer-to-lip-reader distillation (M02) is ahead of the prior record and repeats over two datasets and three teachers; the audio rationale is untested and the LRS2 state-of-the-art claim fails.
position: The paper [@zhao2020hearing] changes the training-only supervision (M02): a speech recognizer is distilled into a sentence-level lip reader at three granularities, transcripts kept. Before 2019-05, audio entered sentence-level lip-reader training as forced-alignment targets (13 of 77 decoders) and never as distilled teacher outputs (0 of 77, pattern match, Appendix), so the design is ahead at the time, shared with the [concurrent] Afouras et al. [@afouras2020asr]. The gain repeats on CMLR and LRS2 and with all three teachers, each a single value without a run count (§4), but the rationale that the benefit comes from audio is untested: a [later] same-student comparison finds a video teacher at least as useful [@ren2021master]. The state-of-the-art claim (M12) holds for CMLR only; on LRS2 the paper's own Table 5 lists lower WER for two earlier systems.
